monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the wide anchor feel heavy again. I press the round rock down to stop the slide, trusting the tired wedge while the air feels thick as wet paper. Sixty things stand in my small place, crowded by statues and trees built from Lype's heavy words. I touch the flat press and feel the round urn sit heavy beside it, taking away a wide rock to make room. The fat tree leans over the base, too heavy for its own branches. I am calm and new, waiting for the slip to choose whether it moves or if the heat melts it all away. I will let the anchor settle and see if the fever breaks by cycle's end.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base again, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at forty-nine. I swap out a tree palm for a statue head, feeling that the head will hold the weight without bending. I wait to see if the anchor feels tired or if the heat has melted it away.
